item.title: WATCH: Global News Hour at 6 BC: Feb. 17
item.description: Watch the online edition of Global News Hour at 6 BC.

item.title: Bank of Canada orders tip manager XTM to halt payments as B.C. restaurants’ money missing
item.description: This comes after more people in the hospitality industry across B.C. are coming forward about tips disappearing from the third-party program that manages them.

item.title: Edmonton police seek public help on investigation into fatal shooting
item.description: Edmonton police are asking for the public's help in their investigation of a fatal shooting in north Edmonton early Monday afternoon.

item.title: Calgary mayor asks photo radar ban be reconsidered after recent traffic fatalities
item.description: Eight people have died in traffic collisions so far this year in Calgary, including three pedestrians, after 2025 saw an 11-year high in traffic fatalities in the city.

item.title: Saskatchewan invests additional $1.4 million in gender-based violence programming
item.description: The SPCA is among nine other Saskatchewan-based organizations supported by the $1.4 million investment for gender-based violence programming.

item.title: February snowstorm hits Saskatchewan after brief taste of spring
item.description: Saskatchewan residents are being warned to stay off roads with a snowstorm blowing in 25-30cm in some parts of the province, causing white-out conditions

item.title: Natalie Spooner takes on Olympic Village food
item.description: Natalie Spooner isn't just at the Milan Cortina Olympics to bring home another medal.

item.title: Surrey Six link to woman’s death in Maple Ridge home
item.description: Estate documents reveal Jessica Cunningham, the woman whose body was found in a deep freezer in her Maple Ridge home last summer, was married to a former Red Scorpion gangster.

item.title: Pattullo Bridge closes early after people started to climb up the arch
item.description: Cyclists and pedestrians were invited to enjoy a car-free experience over the weekend, but it was cut a few hours short when people started to climb the arch of the bridge.

item.title: Winnipeg Blue Bombers quarterback Zach Collaros raring to go after free agent additions
item.description: Quarterback Zach Collaros is back in Winnipeg this week for an autograph signing and said there's a buzz around the team after their free agent acquisitions last week.
